name: Passing Props
description: Attributes passed to a component are collected into a single `props` object, which the component reads to customize its output.
notes: Non-string values (numbers, objects, booleans, functions) must be wrapped in `{}`.

name: Default Props
description: Provides a fallback value for a prop when the parent doesn't pass one, most commonly done with a default parameter in the function signature.
notes: The static `Component.defaultProps = {...}` assignment still works but is deprecated for function components in favor of default parameters.

name: children as a Prop
description: `children` is just a regular prop that React populates automatically from nested JSX content, enabling wrapper/layout components.

name: Prop Drilling
description: Passing props down through several layers of intermediate components that don't use the data themselves, just to get it to a deeply nested child.
example:
// theme passes through Header even though only Logo needs it
<App theme={theme}>
  <Header theme={theme}>
    <Logo theme={theme} />
  </Header>
</App>
notes: Context, component composition, or state management libraries are common ways to avoid excessive prop drilling.

name: Typing Props with TypeScript
syntax:
type Props = { name: string; onClose?: () => void };
function Modal({ name, onClose }: Props) { ... }
description: Defining a type or interface for a component's props so TypeScript can check what's passed in and enable editor autocompletion.
notes: Use `?` for optional props and prefer explicit types over `React.FC`, which implicitly adds `children` and offers little benefit.

name: Spreading Props
description: Uses the object spread operator to forward all key/value pairs of an object as individual props to a component in one expression.
notes: Convenient for pass-through wrapper components, but can obscure exactly which props a component accepts — use deliberately.

name: Props are Read-Only
description: A component must never mutate its own props; React treats components as pure functions of their props, and mutating them breaks that contract.
notes: If a child needs to change data owned by a parent, the parent should pass a callback prop instead of letting the child mutate props directly.

name: PropTypes
description: A runtime type-checking library for React props, from the separate `prop-types` package, used mainly in JavaScript (non-TypeScript) codebases.
notes: Only warns in development via the console; TypeScript is generally preferred for compile-time prop checking in new projects.
